To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proliferation and differentiation of HPCs from healthy persons, patients, and CML patients were regulated by cyclic nucleotides in a concentration-dependent fashion, and the reaction patterns of these HPCs were heterogeneous.
the cyclic nucleotide-regulated PKA and PKG pathways in human hematopoiesis vary in healthy donors and patients with hematopoietic diseases, including chronic myelocyticleukemia.
HPCs from healthy persons, patients suffering from tumors, and CML patients show different proliferation and differentiation patterns when stimulated with cyclic nucleotide-elevation agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new therapeutic approach for HPC recovery and expansion.
the development of a novel therapeutic approach in the treatment of patients with hematopoietic disorders.
the regulation of proliferation and differentiation of HPCs from healthy persons, patients suffering from tumor diseases, or CML patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of cGMP and cAMP are not only dependent on the source of HCPs but also on the concentration of the cyclic nucleotides and the time of stimulation.
the cyclic nucleotide-elevation of HPCs is dependent on the source of HCPs and that cyclic nucleotides can be used to control the proliferation and differentiation of HCPs.

the effects of cyclic AMP and guanosine monophsophate on hematopoietic stem cell growth and differentiation are dependent on the source of the cells, and that the effects on growth and differentiation are not always opposite to each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proliferation and differentiation of HPCs is influenced by the source of cells.
cyclic nucleotides are involved in the regulation of HPC proliferation and that the source of HCPs is an important parameter for the interpretation of results obtained from experiments with HPCs.
the proliferation and differentiation of HPCs from healthy donors and tumor patients can be regulated by PKG and PKA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the source of HCPs has a profound impact on the cellular response to cyclic nucleotides.
cyclic nucleotides can be used to regulate the proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic stem cells.
the source of HCPs (healthy vs CML) is an important factor to consider when evaluating the effects of cyclic-nucleotide elevating agents.
